summary:
Technical review of phase:rework-7, iteration 1 (sub-mv4bez91-0173458d; handoffs ho-mv4aker9-014c05a3 and ho-mv4b2qcu-01d596a2; decisions dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af, dec-mv46ovf2-017bf12d as corrected by dec-mv4740d4-015b3589, and dec-mv48g2fj-018e0ca7). Run run-mv4bflas-01f6302a. The security review (.eccode/reviews/drafts/rework-7-security-1.md, FINAL, approve) is folded in.

**Scope.**
- All 19 artifacts match the submitted sha256.
- `git diff 1996afa 1f4e430` gives the 18 project files.
- Every check I cite ran on the submitted tree 51dc3468. The later commit f63d5b1 changes only records.

**My checks are all green.** Real clock: npm test 2341/2333/0 fail/8 skipped, the browser suite 14/14, and the eight changed test files 216/216. With the clock-shift preload: npm test at +9 days (2026-10-20T21:22Z, just past the pin) and at +100 days (2027-01-19) is green, 2341/2333/0/8.

**Your rework-6 findings are resolved against my own resolution conditions:**
- TR-R6-1: my pl-delay mutant is now killed by the re-timed per-call bound. The file is green 3/3 under 12 busy loops on 4 CPUs, and a locked npm test is green.
- TR-R6-2: the comment is corrected.
- TR-R6-4: the one-line no-unlink mutant is killed at shifts of 0, 9, 30, 100 and 400 days, and the real tree is green at each.

**The other items are correct and pinned by tests.** FU-59 per order, FU-58/56, FU-54, FU-55, FU-57, the canonical sentence, FU-21, FU-12 and the README were each checked against the diff and the spec or decision. Nine correctness mutants, each in a fresh copy, are all killed on their own subtests.

**The clock-shift method is sound enough for the claim on the Node side.** My probe confirms it shifts the clock in the test process, in the file-system time paths the code uses, and in child servers. The paths it misses are not used by the code. One finding (TR-R7-1, minor): the preload is outside the repository, so the claim cannot be re-run by the verification gate or by anyone later.

No blocking or major finding. Decision: approve.

criteria.notes:
**Real clock.**
- npm test under the lock: 2341 / 2333 / 0 fail / 8 skipped, NFR5 p95 59.1 ms (ev:ev-mv4biwc1-01d635bc).
- Browser suite under the lock: 14/14 (ev:ev-mv4c3zpy-01b16590).

- +9 days: the child sees 2026-10-20T21:22Z, just past the 2026-10-20T06:00Z pin; npm test 2341/2333/0/8 (ev:ev-mv4bzdu2-012809ac).
- +100 days: the child sees 2027-01-19, past the year boundary; npm test 2341/2333/0/8 (ev:ev-mv4c1nep-01dedc0d).

**The orphan-age boundary test** (uploads-retention L634) pins `clock - mtime` with three files: exactly 1 day old is removed, 1 ms younger is kept, and one stamped after the clock is kept. The engineer's |clock - mtime| mutant is killed (ev:ev-mv49xotr-01551c66).

**My own audit of where real time meets the injected clock in src agrees with item 13.**
- Date.now appears only in systemClock, AI-provider latency defaults, the DB busy-retry deadline and the config default demo date (relative or today-based).
- mtime is used only in retention.js L83 and the static ETag.
- There is no SQL clock: no CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and no datetime('now') in src, migrations or test.
- The client uses only relative time (poll.js).

**TR-R6-1/2/4** are resolved below. **Security** reviewed before delivery: FINAL, approve; see the security criterion.

criteria.description: The clock-shift method is sound enough to support 'nothing breaks once real time passes 2026-10-20' (as asked)
criteria.notes:
**What my probe shows** (ev:ev-mv4bsf9l-018c618e, at +30 days).
- **Shifted:** Date.now and new Date(); statSync; the named `stat` import from node:fs/promises, which is what retention.js uses; the fs.stat callback.
- **Round-trips:** utimes with a Date.
- **Children:** a child spawned through childEnv(baseServerEnv()), the way every test server starts, sees the shifted clock. NODE_OPTIONS is merged, not replaced (node-proc.js L72-L84). CLOCK_SHIFT_DAYS has no RS_ prefix, so server-proc.js L48 does not blank it.

**Gaps.** Two were disclosed by the delivery-lead, and I found two more:
- FileHandle.stat is not shifted;
- a string time passed to utimes does not round-trip;
- Intl.DateTimeFormat().format() with no date reads the unpatched clock;
- calling `Date()` without new throws a TypeError.

None of these paths is used by src, test, scripts or public (grep). The last one would fail loudly rather than hide a problem.

**Children the shift does not reach.** They are built with a minimal env: the rs20 live-refusal checks, seed.test.js runSeed, and start-old-node. I read them. They are either time-irrelevant (refusal exit codes) or pin RS_DEMO_DATE, so running them unshifted hides nothing about date passage.

**Not shifted.** SQLite, which has no clock in use, and Chromium, whose client code uses only relative time.

**Verdict.** Sound enough for the claim on the Node side and on the server side of the browser flows. The remaining weakness is reproducibility: TR-R7-1.

findings.title: The date-robustness claim rests on a clock-shift preload that lives outside the repository, so the verification gate cannot re-run it from the project
findings.detail:
The preload `scratchpad/rework7-tools/shift-clock.mjs` (sha256 e1686fdb) is only in a session scratchpad.

**The claim is supported today.**
- Full suites are green at +9, +30 and +100 days, and uploads-retention at up to +400 (ev:ev-mv4bzdu2-012809ac, ev:ev-mv4c1nep-01dedc0d, ev:ev-mv4bw9lu-01d41ccd).
- My probe shows the preload takes effect where it must (ev:ev-mv4bsf9l-018c618e).

**But the claim cannot be reproduced later.** No project file or npm script can repeat it. A later change could reintroduce a real-time dependence, for example a new mtime comparison or a SQL clock, and nothing in npm test would notice before 2026-10-20.

The preload also has known blind spots: FileHandle.stat, a string time to utimes, Intl's default date, and the `Date()` call form. Today they are unused, and the delivery-lead disclosed the first two; nothing in the project records them.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: the orchestrator routes it (no current task owns test/helpers/**).

Resolved when one of these holds:
- The preload is committed as a reviewed project tool, for example test/helpers/shift-clock.mjs plus an npm script such as `test:shifted` that takes CLOCK_SHIFT_DAYS. Its blind spots are listed in its header. The verification gate re-runs it at a shift past 2026-10-20.
- Or the verification report records that it re-ran the scratch preload, identified by sha256, at a shift past the pin, and lists the blind spots as an accepted residual.

findings.title: Disclosed narrowings accepted: FU-55 audits refund_order 404/422 only, FU-57 counts operations only, and the refusal rule leaves U+200B-200D, FEFF and 061C (SEC-R7-I1 folded in)
findings.detail:
**What is covered.** FU-55's wording was 'every 422 on the fault routes'. The delivered rule covers the money-moving kind; L325 pins the narrower behaviour. FU-57 counts refund_failed operations, not escalated reservations.

**The security reviewer accepts these** (draft, 'FU-55, FU-57, lockfile'), and also rates SEC-R7-I1: misleading words inside a supplier reason, isolated and labelled by g1, residual by design.

**Correctness.** I checked that the narrowed rules are what the code does, and my fu55 and fu57 mutants are killed. The unrefused zero-width characters and U+061C do not reorder text, and g1 isolates the reason when it is shown.
findings.recommendation: No change for this gate. Resolved when the verification report lists the two narrowed follow-ups as delivered with their limits.

findings.title: SEC-R7-I2 confirmed: package-lock.json has no node_modules/fsevents entry for playwright's optional macOS dependency
findings.detail:
**What is missing.** playwright 1.56.1 declares `optionalDependencies: {fsevents: 2.3.2}`. The lock records that dependency in the playwright entry but has no `node_modules/fsevents` package entry, so a macOS install would resolve it outside the integrity pin.

**Impact.** It has no effect on Linux or CI and is development-only. Not demonstrated, because there is no network here.
findings.recommendation: Optional. Resolved when the lock is regenerated from an empty node_modules (npm then records the darwin-only optional entry with its integrity) and the FU-12 scan test still passes, or when the verification report documents the gap.

resolvedFindings.resolution:
**My resolution condition is met in full.**
- **The mutant is killed.** My pl-delay mutant (exact, never throws, holds 300 ms on 49 inputs) was rebuilt in a fresh copy of the current tree. The rework-7 planner-sec-b1 test now kills it in tests 1 and 2: 'the minimum of three, 300.2 ms, still exceeds the per-call bound 50 ms' and '... 300.1 ms ... 100 ms', with no PLANNER_LIMIT (kill-check ev:ev-mv4bq7eu-019cc03d).
- **Stable under contention.** The real file is green 3/3 under 12 busy loops on 4 CPUs, held under the lock: worst 51.0-56.7 ms, catalog p95 18.3-27.7 ms against a limit of 100 (ev:ev-mv4bqi0v-01dfd6b6).
- **A locked npm test is green** (ev:ev-mv4biwc1-01d635bc).
- **Mechanism.** assertUnderBound re-times only calls over the pre-rework bound. The 1000 ms ceiling and the 20 ms sweep p95 stay, and test 3 gained a 100 ms catalog p95 computed from the re-timed minima.

The comment at uploads-retention L748-L752 now cites src/services/retention.js L35 for the row-then-file ordering, and the spec's 'Retention and deletion' (L773) only for what it says. That is my resolution condition. The test is unchanged in behaviour and green in ev:ev-mv4c2pnw-01f4d300.

**What the test now pins.** The 7 d + 1 min test stamps the file with the pinned upload time (L540) and asserts `imageFilesLeft === 0`, `orphans === 0`, no new image.orphan_delete event, and no file of the image left (L556-L561).

**The kill holds at every date.** The engineer's one-line no-unlink mutant, rebuilt by me in a fresh copy, fails that test at real-clock shifts of 0, 9, 30, 100 and 400 days. The real tree passes 42/42 at every shift (kill-check ev:ev-mv4bw9lu-01d41ccd).

Past the pin, the mutant also fails the startApp timer test, as expected.
